options.A: Rs 6,05,000 crore

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement from the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement laid before Parliament under the FRBM Act?

options.A: The Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement sets out the strategic priorities of the Government in the fiscal area for the ensuing year, whereas the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement sets out three-year rolling targets for the specified fiscal indicators
options.B: The Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement sets out three-year rolling targets for specified fiscal indicators, whereas the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement sets out the strategic priorities of the Government in the fiscal area for the ensuing financial year
options.C: Both statements set out three-year rolling targets for specified fiscal indicators, the two being alternative names for the same document
options.D: Both statements are presented only in an election year, along with the Interim Budget

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Debt Service Fund from the Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways?

options.A: The Debt Service Fund is credited with appropriations made from the revenues of the Railways to provide a cushion for meeting debt-service obligations in years when revenues are inadequate, whereas the Depreciation Reserve Fund is charged to the working expenses and finances renewals and replacements of assets
options.B: The Debt Service Fund is credited with the proceeds of market borrowings raised through IRFC, whereas the Depreciation Reserve Fund is credited out of the surplus of the Railways
options.C: The Debt Service Fund finances renewals and replacements of over-aged assets, whereas the Depreciation Reserve Fund services the market borrowings of the Railways
options.D: Both funds are credited out of the surplus (net revenue) of the Railways at the close of the financial year

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'AG Suspense' from 'PSB Suspense' in railway accounts?

options.A: AG Suspense is operated for transactions with the accredited public sector bank, whereas PSB Suspense is operated for adjustments with State Governments
options.B: AG Suspense is operated only in the books of the Railway Board, whereas PSB Suspense is operated only by the production units
options.C: AG Suspense is operated for adjustments of transactions between the Railways and the State Governments/Accountants General, whereas PSB Suspense is operated for transactions with the accredited public sector bank, pending settlement or receipt of the bank's advice
options.D: Both heads are operated for transactions with the Reserve Bank of India pending its advice

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Budget document 'Key to Budget Documents' from the 'Expenditure Profile'?

options.A: The Key to Budget Documents presents a snapshot of the pattern of the total expenditure of the Government, whereas the Expenditure Profile explains the terms used in the Budget documents
options.B: The Key to Budget Documents contains the detailed estimates of the Ministry of Railways, whereas the Expenditure Profile contains the recommendations of the Finance Commission
options.C: Both documents explain, clause by clause, the provisions contained in the Finance Bill
options.D: The Key to Budget Documents explains the various other Budget documents and the terms used in them, whereas the Expenditure Profile presents a snapshot (broad overview) of the pattern of the total expenditure of the Government, ministry-wise and scheme-wise

q: For a service of great magnitude whose character is so indefinite that the demand for it cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Demand for Grant, Parliament makes a grant which is often described as a 'blank cheque' to the Government. The grant so made is a:

options.A: Vote on Account
options.C: Exceptional Grant

q: After a grant is voted by Parliament, a zonal railway distributes the amount among its divisions and other spending units so that expenditure can be incurred by them. This distribution of the voted grant among the spending units and offices is known as:

options.A: Budget Allotment
options.C: Re-appropriation

q: A finance officer describes a figure as the aggregate capital invested in the Railways, forming the base of its capital structure, with reference to which the financial results of the Railways are assessed. The figure he is referring to is the:

options.A: Block Account
options.C: Capital-at-charge

q: On the last day allotted for the voting of the Demands for Grants, the Speaker puts all the outstanding Demands together to the vote of the Lok Sabha, whether they have been discussed or not. This practice is known as:

options.A: Guillotine
options.C: Vote on Account

q: A particular budget of the Railways is framed not independently but on the basis of the requirements of the consuming departments and the programme of works, and is for that reason described as a 'derived' budget. The budget so described is the:

options.A: Earnings Budget
options.C: Revenue Budget

q: A clerk preparing the Budget papers for the year 2019-20 proposes to continue showing the expenditure of the Government under the two categories of 'Plan' and 'Non-Plan'. The correct position is that this distinction in the Government Budget was discontinued with effect from the financial year:

A parliamentary committee consisting of twenty-two members — fifteen drawn from the Lok Sabha and seven from the Rajya Sabha — takes up for examination the reports and accounts of the railway public sector undertakings, together with the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on them. The committee so described is the:

options.A: Public Accounts Committee
options.C: Committee on Public Undertakings
options.D: Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways

q: While framing the estimates of a Ministry, the related receipts are not deducted from the expenditure, and the estimates are presented in full, without any netting off. The principle of Government budgeting followed in doing so is:

options.A: Gross budgeting
options.C: Unity of the Budget

q: A consignment is booked at a station of one zonal railway for a destination on another railway, and the freight is collected by the booking railway. In the apportionment of earnings, these through-traffic earnings are initially brought to account in full by:

options.A: The Railway Board, which thereafter divides them among the railways concerned
options.B: The railway on which the traffic originates, that is, the collecting railway, and are thereafter divided among the railways concerned
options.C: The railway at which the traffic terminates
options.D: The Traffic Accounts Office of the destination railway alone

q: In the classification of a capital work financed from the Development Fund, a clerk proposes to indicate the source of finance as the Plan Head of the work. The correct position is that the source from which a work is financed (Capital, DRF, Development Fund, RRSK etc.) is indicated in its classification as its:

options.A: Primary Unit
options.C: Allocation

q: Apart from recommending the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the committee chaired by Bibek Debroy recommended the setting up of an independent regulator for the Railways. The regulator so recommended is the:

options.A: Rail Development Authority
options.C: Railway Claims Tribunal

q: Midway through a financial year, it is found that the amount of a grant voted by Parliament needs to be increased. The increase in the amount of the grant can be effected only by:

options.A: An order of the Railway Board issued with the concurrence of the Financial Commissioner
options.B: Re-appropriation of savings available under another grant
options.C: An order of the Ministry of Finance issued under the General Financial Rules
options.D: A Supplementary Grant voted by Parliament

q: The Demands for Grants having been voted and the Appropriation Bill having been passed by both Houses of Parliament, the Bill becomes the Appropriation Act on receiving the assent of:

options.A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Finance Minister
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

q: At the end of a month, a station renders to the Traffic Accounts Office a statement accounting for all its traffic transactions of the month and showing the balance due from the station. The statement so rendered is the:

options.A: Traffic Book
options.C: Station Balance Sheet

q: In his Budget Speech, the Finance Minister first gives an overview of the economy and announces the major policies of the Government, before turning to the other part of the speech. The part of the Budget Speech in which this overview and the major policy announcements are given is:

options.A: Part A
options.C: Part C

q: An Accounts Officer proposes that a separate appropriation by Parliament must be obtained before any amount can be withdrawn from the accumulated balance of the Depreciation Reserve Fund of a zonal railway. The correct position in this regard is that:

options.A: A separate appropriation by Parliament is required for every withdrawal from the Fund
options.B: No such separate appropriation is required, the balances of the Railway Funds being held in the Public Account of India and not lapsing at the close of the financial year
options.C: A withdrawal can be made only with the prior sanction of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: No withdrawal can be made at all, since the balance of the Fund lapses at the close of the financial year

q: At the close of a financial year, balances are outstanding under certain suspense and remittance heads of a zonal railway, pending clearance. The correct treatment of these outstanding balances is that they:

options.A: Lapse to the Government at the close of the year
options.B: Are written off automatically at the close of the year
options.C: Are transferred to the Railway Pension Fund
options.D: Are carried forward to the next financial year for clearance

q: Under the door-step banking arrangement, the accredited bank collects the earnings of stations and deposits them in the Railways' current account maintained for the purpose. The account into which the collections are so deposited is styled the:

options.A: Rail Shakti Account
options.C: Rail Setu Account

q: A zonal railway expects to receive its budget allotment for a financial year as soon as the Budget is presented to Parliament. Ordinarily, the budget allotment for the year is communicated by the Railway Board to the zonal railways:

options.A: Before the presentation of the Budget in Parliament
options.B: Along with the Revised Estimates in September
options.C: After the Appropriation Act for the year has been passed
options.D: Only at the Final Modification stage in January

q: The estimates of earnings of a zonal railway are first framed by its operating and commercial departments. Before these estimates are adopted in the Budget, they are scrutinised by the:

options.A: Railway Board's Traffic Directorate alone, without any accounts scrutiny
options.C: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

q: Under exchequer control, the expenditure of the Ministries and Departments of the Government during the year is regulated through:

options.A: Budget proportions fixed by the Railway Board
options.C: The Appropriation Accounts of the previous year
options.D: Monthly Expenditure Plans and Quarterly Expenditure Plans

q: The Operating Ratio of a zonal railway for a year is 90 per cent and its net revenue (surplus) for the year is Rs 550 crore. The gross earnings of the railway for the year are:

options.A: Rs 5,500 crore
options.C: Rs 6,100 crore

q: The fiscal deficit of the Government for a year is Rs 11,50,000 crore and its primary deficit for the year is Rs 7,00,000 crore. The interest payments of the Government during the year are:

options.A: Rs 18,50,000 crore
options.C: Rs 7,00,000 crore

q: The sanctioned amount of an imprest held by an officer is Rs 18,000. At a surprise check, the cash in hand with the holder is Rs 5,200. The amount of the paid vouchers held by him in support of the expenditure incurred out of the imprest, and not yet recouped, is:

The annual appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund on account of an asset of the Railways, assessed with reference to the original cost of the asset and its prescribed (codal) life, amounts to Rs 15,000, the codal life of the asset being 25 years. The original cost of the asset is:

The total lease charges payable by the Railways to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation for a year are Rs 13,200 crore, of which the capital (principal) component is Rs 7,800 crore. The interest (finance charge) component of the lease charges for the year is:

options.A: Rs 7,800 crore
options.C: Rs 4,600 crore
